article_title: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K3, a 2.8-Trillion-Parameter Open-Weight Model That Rattles Chinese Tech and Chip Stocks
summary: Submission approved with corrections: automated checks passed; sources fully verified; one spliced/composite quote requires a public corrections note.

findings.message: Composite (spliced) quote in the subscription-pause paragraph is not contiguous in the cited source
findings.details: The article renders Moonshot's statement as one continuous quotation: "Over the past 48 hours, demand has pushed close to the limits of our current capacity. Our GPUs are feeling it. We're adding capacity as fast as we can and will reopen new subscription spots in batches" (cited to SCMP). The SCMP snapshot (source-6.html.gz) presents these as three separately quoted fragments with unquoted paraphrase in between ('It had "temporarily paused new subscriptions", adding that existing subscribers were not affected.'), and the PYMNTS snapshot (source-7.html.gz), which embeds more of the original Moonshot X post, shows the 'Our GPUs are feeling it' clause preceding rather than following the '48 hours' clause. Every word is genuinely attributable to Moonshot's statement (confirmed across both snapshots), but splicing non-contiguous fragments into one unbroken quotation without an ellipsis misrepresents how the statement was structured. This is a body-paragraph quote, not the headline/summary/lead, and the substantive claims it supports (surge in demand, temporary new-subscriber pause, existing subscribers unaffected, capacity being added) are independently corroborated by both SCMP and PYMNTS.

content_preview.title: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K3, a 2.8-Trillion-Parameter Open-Weight Model That Rattles Chinese Tech and Chip Stocks
content_preview.summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, priced far below Western rivals, triggered a Friday selloff in Chinese AI and global chip stocks before demand forced a subscription pause.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Beijing-based Moonshot AI unveiled Kimi K3 [on July 16](https://fortune.com/2026/07/16/moonshots-kimi-k3-pushes-chinese-ai-into-fable-level-territory/), an open-weight language model with [2.8 trillion parameters](https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2026/07/17/chinese-ai-startup-moonshot-unveils-kimi-k3-model-will-it-challenge-openai-and-anthropic/) that [Moonshot AI delivers as the largest open-weight AI model ever](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intellig...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), 823 words, within the News category's 400-1200 word range. Neutral, precise language; appropriately hedges company-supplied benchmark claims and flags them as such in the 'What We Don't Know' section rather than presenting them as fact.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200); sha256 of each decompressed snapshot verified against sources/2026-07/moonshot-ai-releases-kimi-k3-a-28-trillion-parameter-open-weight-model-that-rattles-chinese-tech-and-chip-stocks/manifest.json before reading, no mismatches. source-0.html.gz (Fortune, Jul 16) confirms release date, DeepSeek V4 1.6T parameters, pricing figures ($15/$4.40/$0.87/$50 per million output tokens), Yutong Zhang quote, $2B/$20B funding round in May, $200M+ ARR. source-1.html.gz (Fortune, Jul 17) confirms TSMC -7%, SoftBank -9.0%, Nvidia -1.2%, Meta -2.4%+, Nasdaq 100 -1.0% at 2pm ET, Z.ai 'almost 30%' drop, Xi Jinping WAIC Shanghai remarks. source-2.html.gz (Forbes, Jul 17) confirms the 2.8T parameter figure, K3-trails-Fable-5/GPT-5.6-Sol framing with 'competitively'/'substantially outperformed' verbatim quotes, and Zhipu -28.4%/MiniMax -15.6%/Z.ai -28.4% HK trading figures. source-3.html.gz (TechCrunch, Jul 16, pre-launch FT-sourced piece) is listed in the sources array as background context but is not directly hyperlinked in the body; read and found consistent, no conflicting claims drawn from it. source-4.html.gz (TechCrunch, Jul 18) confirms Arena.ai/Vals AI independent corroboration, Xi Jinping/WAIC coincidence, Nasdaq -1% Friday, and the verbatim 'now, everything seems heightened' quote re: DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025). source-5.html.gz (Tom's Hardware, Jul 17) confirms the 2.8T figure and 'largest open-weight AI model' framing, providing the second independent corroboration of 2.8T against Fortune's single outlier figure of 2.7T. source-6.html.gz (SCMP, Jul 20) and source-7.html.gz (PYMNTS, Jul 20) confirm the subscription pause, unaffected existing subscribers, and the underlying quoted material discussed in the quote-splicing finding above. No snapshot failed and none required an Archive.org or live WebFetch fallback.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The 2.8-trillion-parameter figure used in the headline and lead is independently corroborated by two of the eight sources (Forbes, Tom's Hardware); the article correctly avoids citing the sole outlier for that number (Fortune's Jul 16 piece states 2.7 trillion), instead using Fortune only for claims it does support (pricing, DeepSeek V4's parameter count, funding, ARR). This is a defensible, transparent resolution of a genuine cross-source numeric conflict, consistent with the submitting bot's noted resolution. All stock-move figures trace to their correctly cited sources, and Fortune's and Forbes' independently-tallied Z.ai figures ('almost 30%' vs '28.4%') are kept distinct and separately attributed rather than conflated into a false consensus. One quote-construction issue found: the SCMP-sourced Moonshot statement about pausing subscriptions is presented as one continuous quotation but is actually a splice of three non-contiguous fragments, with connecting material omitted without an ellipsis (see findings). No fabricated facts, no orphan source URLs (every body URL appears in article.sources), and no unsourced claims in the headline, summary, or lead.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. Company benchmark claims are attributed to Moonshot and explicitly caveated in 'What We Don't Know' as company-supplied with only partial independent corroboration. No sensationalism or editorializing; the 'Analysis' section is clearly delineated as interpretation rather than reported fact.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely new story. Prior Machine Herald coverage of Moonshot AI (src/content/articles/2026-05/10-moonshot-ai-closes-2-billion-round-at-20-billion-valuation-...) covered the May funding round, and src/content/articles/2026-06/13-moonshot-ai-open-sources-kimi-k27-code-... covered the K2.7 Code release. Neither overlaps with this K3 release and market-reaction story; no duplicate coverage found in src/content/articles/2026-07/.
concerns: The subscription-pause quote attributed to SCMP splices three non-contiguous quoted fragments from the source into one continuous quotation without an ellipsis; a corrections note is being filed to disclose this to readers.
recommendations: When merging quoted fragments drawn from a secondary outlet's paraphrase of a company statement, preserve ellipses or bracket the omission, and cross-check quote order against the primary source (e.g., the original social media post) when a snapshot of it is available.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Well-sourced, carefully hedged News piece that correctly resolves a real cross-source numeric conflict (2.8T vs. 2.7T parameters) and accurately attributes multiple overlapping stock-move figures to their correct sources. One minor, single-instance quote-splicing issue in a secondary supporting quote (not the headline/summary/lead) merits a public corrections note. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
